runs.text: Write between 2 and 4 test cases for the 40-seat bus program, so that any wrong version fails at least one of them.

hints.text: A case uncovers a wrong version if, with that input, the version shows something else. Which inputs tell one version from another?
Think about the zones: pupils that fill the buses exactly, and pupils left over by a little or by a lot.
You need at least one case where the division is exact and another where a few are left over.
95 → 3 uncovers the one that does not round; 80 → 2 uncovers the one that adds one too many. Close with the variant.

runs.text: Is there a single input that uncovers all three wrong versions at once? (No: 81 → 3 uncovers two of them, but not the one that adds one too many.)
Wrong versions: no rounding, one too many, and rounding to the nearest. Rounding to the nearest falls with any case where a few are left over, such as 81 or 95.
